Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

federal adjective

also federation, federal state, confederation, confederate, federal government

classical

Cic. Arch. 7: sī quī foederātīs cīvitātibus ascrīptī fuissent
Traupman 180

foederātus, foederāta, foederātum

declension

bound by treaty, allied; federal

Classically of a people bound to Rome by a treaty, foedus (Lewis & Short, s.v. foederō). Used now of the members of a federation; the United States are Cīvitātēs Foederātae (Traupman 180).

Other words

  • cīvitās foederāta — a federal state; a state of the United States

    also used · modern · Traupman 180

    A modern application of the classical word; our sources give no settled term for the federal government as against the states’ (see state, a country).

Examples

  • data est cīvitās Silvānī lēge et Carbōnis: sī quī foederātīs cīvitātibus ascrīptī fuissent

    citizenship was given by the law of Silvanus and Carbo to any who had been enrolled in allied citiesCic. Arch. 7

See also state, government, agreement.
